info.title: VMRay Platform REST API
info.description:
You can use this interface to execute REST API requests directly.

1. Obtain your **VMRay Platform API key**. See documentation `API Programmer Guide > Creating API Calls`.
2. Click the **Authorize** button.
3. Enter the value in the format: `api_key <VMRAY_API_KEY>`
4. Click **Authorize** again to confirm.

After authorization, you can send requests to the VMRay Platform through this API client.

get.description:
Retrieve the Analysis Archive of a given analysis. You can either specify the Analysis ID or the Job ID of
 the analysis. The latter can be used to save an additional API request if the Analysis ID is not known but
 the job ID is.
 


 The Analysis Archive that is returned is a standard ZIP file. It is possible to retrieve one or more
 individual files instead of the full archive using the **filename** and **filenames** parameters.
 Wildcards (* and ?) are supported when using the **filenames** parameter. For example, you could
 retrieve all extracted files in the archive (extracted_files/*).
 


 Retrieving all screenshot files in the archive can be done in the same way, by using the **filenames**
 parameter and passing screenshots/*.
 However, screenshots can also be downloaded directly using the **filename** parameter set to just
 'screenshots'. Part of screenshot files is 'index.log', which contains meta information about available
 screenshots in the following format:
 '{timedelta} | {size} | md5={md5},sha1={sha1},sha256={sha256} | {screenshot_filename}'.
 


 Ensure that you encode slashes correctly. The **filenames** parameter allows the return of a
 filtered archive that only holds certain files. File names must be separated using commas.
 The archive might be password-protected depending on the user settings.
 Check the Console or the API for the password.
 


 
ℹ️ 
 Note that downloading the screenshots is possible even if the Analysis Report is locked in the Console.
 



**Examples**

Retrieve the full ZIP Archive of Analysis ID **123**:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Retrieve the full ZIP Archive of Analysis ID **123** encrypted with a password:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?encryption_password=L8XYM9eJhCWkoMBkmLkH' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Retrieve only the **flog.xml** file of Analysis ID **123** (this does not return a ZIP file but the XML file itself):
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive/logs%2fflog.xml' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > flog.xml
```
Retrieve only the **stix-report-2-1.json** file of Analysis ID **123** (this does not return a ZIP file but the JSON file itself):
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive/report%2fstix-report-2-1.json' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > stix-report-2-1.json
```
Return the ZIP archive with only **worker.log** and **post_process.log**:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filenames=logs%2Fworker.log%2Clogs%2Fpost_process.log' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Return the ZIP archive with only the **extracted_files**:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filenames=extracted_files%2F%2A' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Return the ZIP archive with all IOCs in CSV format:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filenames=report%2Fartifacts%2F%2Aiocs.csv' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Return the ZIP archive with all artifacts in CSV format:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filenames=report%2Fartifacts%2F%2Aartifacts.csv' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > analysis.zip
```
Return all IOCs in CSV format:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filename=report%2Fartifacts%2Fall_iocs.csv' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > all_iocs.csv
```
Return all artifacts in CSV format:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filename=report%2Fartifacts%2Fall_artifacts.csv' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > all_artifacts.csv
```
Return the ZIP archive with only the **screenshots/**:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filename=screenshots' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > screenshots.zip
```
Download only individual screenshots for a specific analysis:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filename=screenshots%2F7200a1be57f96d7110f6b7beb306bf869b4be729.png' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > 7200a1be57f96d7110f6b7beb306bf869b4be729.png
```
Download only individual screenshots for a specific analysis and the index.log. The index.log holds meta information about the screenshot files. Also it shows the order in which screenshots were taken:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/123/archive?filenames=screenshots%2F7200a1be57f96d7110f6b7beb306bf869b4be729.png%2Cscreenshots%2Findex.log' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    > screenshots.zip
```

get.description:
Retrieve analyses based on their properties. The search criteria is specified inside of the
 query parameter **query** using a simple query language with the following structure:

 `<field> <operator> <value>`

 or in case of multiple values

 `<field> <operator> <value> <connector> <field> <operator> <value> <connector> ...`

 There can be up to 5 filters.
 
 **Search criteria**
 


 
 **Field:**

 `field` can have the following values and allows the following `operators`:
 
 * filename: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * threat_name: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * url: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 
 


 
 **Value:**

 If the value contains whitespaces it needs to be wrapped in double quotes (`""`).
 


 
 **Connector:**

 `connector` can be one of the following:
 
 * 'and': logical and
 * 'or': logical or
 
 Note that the 'and' has a higher precedence.
 


 
 **Operator:**

 `operator` can be one of the following:
 
 * '==': an equal match (case insensitive)
 * '<>': a not equal match (case insensitive)
 * 'like': a similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 * 'not like': a not similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 
 



**Examples**

Retrieve all analyses that have the threat name *Threat1*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all analyses that have the threat name *Threat with whitespaces*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+%22Threat+with+whitespaces%22' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all analyses that have both threat names: *Threat1* **and** *Threat2*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1+and+threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat2' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all analyses that have either threat names: *Threat1* **or** *Threat2*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1+or+threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat2' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all analyses that have a threat name starting with: *Threat*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/search?query=threat_name+like+Threat%25' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```

post.description:
Add a tag to analysis with a specified ID.
 The maximum length of a tag is limited to 255 characters. Only Unicode letters, digits, and these special
 characters are allowed: _ . ! ? ; : + – = / $ @ % ^ & ) ( \# '\\' and '-'.

**Examples**

Add the tag **foo** to Analysis ID **456**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/analysis/456/tag?tag_name=foo' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```

Create a new API key assigned to the user with an ID specified in the **api_key_user_id** parameter.
 The API key authorization string and name will be autogenerated and returned in the request's response.
 Note that the hashed API key will only be returned once after creation and **won't
 be** accessible afterwards.

**Examples**

Create a new API key for User ID **123**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/api_key' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    -F api_key_user_id=123
```
Create a new API key for User ID **123**:

Retrieve samples based on their properties. The search criteria is specified inside of the
 query parameter **query** using a simple query language with the following structure:

 `<field> <operator> <value>`

 or in case of multiple values

 `<field> <operator> <value> <connector> <field> <operator> <value> <connector> ...`

 There can be up to 10 filters.
 
 **Search criteria**
 


 
 **Field:**

 `field` can have the following values and allows the following `operators`:
 
 * filename: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * threat_name: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * url: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * vti_classification: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 
 


 
 **Value:**

 If the value contains whitespaces it needs to be wrapped in double quotes (`""`).
 


 
 **Connector:**

 `connector` can be one of the following:
 
 * 'and': logical and
 * 'or': logical or
 
 Note that the 'and' has a higher precedence.
 


 
 **Operator:**

 `operator` can be one of the following:
 
 * '==': an equal match (case insensitive)
 * '<>': a not equal match (case insensitive)
 * 'like': a similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 * 'not like': a not similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 
 



**Examples**

```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
```

 **cmd_line** parameter.
 


 If a container sample type is submitted, then the **archive_action** or **disk_image_action**
 parameters determine whether Archive or macOS DMG should be treated as a sample, compound sample or
 as separate samples. Supported parameter values are
 
 * **sample** — container is treated as a sample
 * **compound_sample** — container is treated as compound sample with automatically selected entry point
 (**entry_point** allows you to override which file in the container is the main file that should be
 executed)
 * **separate_samples** — every file in the container is treated as a separate submission
 
 The **user analyzer** setting is used as the default value for this parameter.
 


 If a password protected archive is submitted using an uncommon sample password, then the parameter
 **archive_password** must specify the password.
 


 By default, submitted files create new jobs according to the default Jobrules of the sample type. This
 parameter **jobrule_entries** can be used to specify alternative Jobrules to be used for this submission
 instead. The parameter can either be a JSON dictionary or a JSON list:

 1. Dictionary: The keys must be Jobrule name and the values must be Jobrule entry signatures that should
 be used for this sample type.

 2. List: This must be a list of Jobrule entry signatures, which is used no matter what the sample
 type is.

 Note that you cannot define new Jobrules in the provided dictionary. Jobrules for the specified
 sample types must already exist in the system. A list of available Jobrules and Jobrule entry signatures can
 be found in the Analysis Settings in the Web Interface.
 


 To ensure a smooth analysis, the sample filename should only contain valid characters.
 
 * Windows filenames usually can't contain: ':', '<', '>', '\', '"', '|', '?', '*', '/' and the
 values from 0x00 to 0x1F. If you submit a filename containing at least one of these characters,
 the filename will be automatically sanitized. The filename will be replaced with a random string.
 * In addition, files with DOS device filenames will be automatically sanitized as well,
 this affects the following filenames: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1, COM2, COM3, COM4, COM5, COM6, COM7,
 COM8, COM9, LPT1, LPT2, LPT3, LPT4, LPT5, LPT6, LPT7, LPT8, LPT9.
 * On macOS, the following characters are not allowed in filenames: ':', '/', 0x00.
 * For Linux, the following characters are usually forbidden: '/', 0x00. Filenames submitted containing
 these characters will be automatically sanitized according to the procedure for Windows.
 
 


 URL samples must not start with the following characters: 0x21 to 0x7E.
 


 The **prescript_file** parameter specifies an optional Prescript to be used.
 


 The **prescript_force_admin** parameter indicates whether Prescript files should be run with Administrator
 rights.
 


 The **sample_type** is an optional parameter that can be used to overwrite the sample type auto
 detection of the VMRay Platform. The specified sample type is then enforced. Supported strings
 are shown in the "Sample Type" listbox in the Console when submitting a sample. Be aware that
 the sample type parameter for compound samples with API submissions is ignored. In that case,
 the sample type's entrypoint is detected automatically.
 


 The **shareable** parameter indicates whether the hash of the sample will be shared with VirusTotal.
 


 The **enable_reputation** parameter indicates whether Reputation Analysis should be performed for
 submitted samples and analysis artifacts (file hashes and URLs) by the VMRay Platform and
 additional third party services. Please note that in the case of files, only hash values are
 transmitted and not the file itself. The **user analyzer** setting is used as the default value for this
 parameter.
 


 The **analyzer_mode** parameter specifies which types of analyses should be used for analyzing this
 sample.
 Supported strings are
 
 * **reputation**
 * **reputation_static**
 * **reputation_static_dynamic**
 * **static_dynamic**
 * **static**
 
 The **user analyzer** setting is used as the default value for this parameter.
 


 The **known_malicious** parameter specifies if Triage should be used to pre-filter known malicious
 samples based on the results of Reputation Analysis (if allowed) and Static Analysis.
 The **user analyzer** setting is used as the default value for this parameter.
 


 The **known_benign** parameter specifies if Triage should be used to pre-filter known benign
 samples based on the results of Reputation Analysis (if allowed) and Static Analysis.
 The **user analyzer** setting is used as the default value for this parameter.
 


 The **analysis_caching** parameter allows you to reuse cached analyses and jobs when resubmitting a
 sample. Supported values are
 
 * **disabled**
 * **enabled**
 * **smart**
 * **legacy**
 
 Users can select the option they prefer with the Analysis Caching option which is available on the Analysis
 Settings page.
 


 The **user_config** parameter allows you to overwrite certain configuration settings for this submission.
 Please note that standard users may only overwrite a few configuration settings, whereas Administrators are
 not restricted. Refer to the Administrator configuration APIs for a list of available configuration
 parameters. This parameter can be used to specify a Network Scheme.
 


 The **disable_known_config** parameter allows you to deny the use of configuration parameters for samples
 that are known to VMRay Platform.
 


 The **dll_calls** parameter allows you to specify a list of DLL calls that will be executed if a DLL sample
 is submitted. This list must contain the strings that describe the names of certain DLL functions and
 their arguments if required. Note that the **dll_calls** parameter string must be url encoded.
 If this parameter is not provided, all available DLL functions will be called by default.
 


 The **dll_call_mode** parameter describes how DLL functions will be executed. You can specify either
 **separated** or **single** values in combination with the **dll_calls** parameter.
 **Separated** mode means that every DLL function will be executed in a separate process while **single**
 means consistent execution of all functions within one process. Also, there are **load_library** and
 **fuzzing** modes which must be specified without the **dll_calls** parameter. If neither
 **dll_call_mode** nor **dll_calls** parameters are specified, **fuzzing** mode will be
 applied by default.
 **fuzzing** mode means that analysis will call every exported function from the DLL library with different
 arguments. If **load_library** is specified, only the main function will be called.
 


 The optional **max_jobs** parameter limits the amount of jobs that can be created by Jobrules for this
 submission. With an activated billing system, this parameter allows you to control the consumption
 of the Quota.
 


 The **tags** parameter can be used to specify a comma-separated list of tags for this submission. The maximum
 length of a tag is limited to 255 characters. Only Unicode letters, digits, and these special characters
 are allowed: _ . ! ? ; : + – = / $ @ % ^ & ) ( \# '\\' and '-'.
 


 The **document_password** parameter specifies an optional document password to analyze password-protected
 documents.
 


 The **system_time** parameter specifies an optional analysis system date and time setting.
 


 The **retention_period** parameter specifies the amount of time before submissions are automatically
 deleted from the server. This includes the submitted samples and related analyses. The following periods
 (in days) are supported: 0, 60, 120, 180, 360. A 0 value means data is not automatically deleted.
 


 The **submission_metadata** parameter specifies the JSON dictionary of additional parameters.
 


 The **child_relations** parameter specifies the JSON list of **sample_id** and **relation_type** pairs
 which define the child samples.
 


 The **sample_url** parameter specifies a URL for Web Analysis.
 


 The **webhook_notification** parameter specifies an optional JSON dictionary to enable a webhook notification
 for this submission. It will be triggered once all analyses for this submission have either run successfully
 or failed permanently. The dictionary supports these entries
 
 * **url**: A string with the URL the POST should be sent to. Must have a http or https scheme.
 It is strongly recommended to use https.
 * **verify_tls**: An optional boolean to control whether the server should verify the TLS certificate
 for an URL with https scheme. Defaults to true.
 * **timeout**: An optional number of seconds that specifies the connection timeout to use for the
 webhook target. Defaults to 10 seconds.
 * **retries**: An optional integer that specifies the number of retries to attempt in case delivery
 of the webhook fails. Retries are attempted with an exponential backoff scheme. Defaults to 2.
 * **headers**: An optional dictionary that contains additional headers that should be set in the
 POST request.
 
 


 The **ai_based_phishing_detection** parameter allows you to configure the AI Engine for Phishing.
 Supported values are
 
 * **disabled**: Rely on conventional detection mechanisms.
 * **conservative**: Require high confidence for detections.
 * **normal**: Strike a balance between confidence and sensitivity.
 * **aggressive**: Enable maximum sensitivity.
 
 


 The API returns a dictionary with these lists:
 
 * **errors**: List of all files which caused errors during submission.
 * **jobs**: List of all Dynamic or Web Analysis jobs that were created.
 * **static_jobs**: List of all Static Analysis jobs that were created.
 Note that these jobs share the same structure with dynamic jobs.
 * **reputation_jobs**: List of all Reputation jobs that were created.
 * **whois_jobs**: List of all WHOIS jobs that were created.
 * **md_jobs**: This field is deprecated and always returns an empty list.
 * **vt_jobs**: List of all VirusTotal jobs that were created.
 * **samples**: List of all samples that were created or referenced.
 * **submissions**: List of all submissions that were created.
 
 


 If an archive was submitted, the **submission_filename** field in result datasets can be used to
 match the file name in the archive to the created sample entry.
 



**Examples**

Submit **sample.exe**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/sample/submit' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
    -F sample_file=@sample.exe
```
Retrieve **sample.exe** from a remote HTTP server and submit it:
```bash

```

```bash
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>' \
```

Submit **sample.zip** as a compound sample with an entry point of **sample.exe**:

Submit **sample.zip** as a separate sample:

Submit **sample.exe** with a Prescript ID of **123**:

get.description:
Retrieve submissions based on their properties. The search criteria is specified inside of the
 query parameter **query** using a simple query language with the following structure:

 `<field> <operator> <value>`

 or in case of multiple values

 `<field> <operator> <value> <connector> <field> <operator> <value> <connector> ...`

 There can be up to 10 filters.
 
 **Search criteria**
 


 
 **Field:**

 `field` can have the following values and allows the following `operators`:
 
 * filename: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * threat_name: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 * url: '==', '<>', 'like' and 'not like'
 
 


 
 **Value:**

 If the value contains whitespaces it needs to be wrapped in double quotes (`""`).
 


 
 **Connector:**

 `connector` can be one of the following:
 
 * 'and': logical and
 * 'or': logical or
 
 Note that the 'and' has a higher precedence.
 


 
 **Operator:**

 `operator` can be one of the following:
 
 * '==': an equal match (case insensitive)
 * '<>': a not equal match (case insensitive)
 * 'like': a similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 * 'not like': a not similar match. Use '%' as a wildcard
 
 



**Examples**

Retrieve all submissions that have the threat name *Threat1*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/submission/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all submissions that have the threat name *Threat with whitespaces*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/submissions/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+%22Threat+with+whitespaces%22' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all submissions that have both threat names: *Threat1* **and** *Threat2*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/submission/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1+and+threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat2' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all submissions that have either threat names: *Threat1* **or** *Threat2*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/submission/search?query=threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat1+or+threat_name+%3D%3D+Threat2' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Retrieve all submissions that have a threat name starting with: *Threat*:
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/submission/search?query=threat_name+like+Threat%25' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```

ℹ️ 
 Depending on the licensed product and product plan, there might be restrictions when using certain
 YARA endpoints.
 

Create a YARA Ruleset.
 


 
ℹ️ 
 **Uploading Long YARA Rulesets**
 
 * The maximum allowed length of YARA rulesets that can be uploaded via the API using the
 **yara_ruleset_rules** parameter is 10,485,760 characters or approximately 10MB in size.
 * Due to restrictions within CURL, direct submission of arguments of this length is not feasible.
 Therefore, uploading YARA rulesets of this size would require the utilization of an external
 program.
 * To upload YARA rulesets approaching the maximum limit, we recommend providing the
 parameters in the body rather than as query parameters.

post.description:
Editing other user's YARA Rulesets requires Account Manager privileges. Some
 parameters also require Account Manager privileges. See below for details.
 


 **name**, **rules** and **owner_user_id** update the respective parts of the selected YARA
 Rule. **owner_user_id** may only be updated by Account Managers and Administrators.
 


 The parameter **type** can be set to either **Shared** or **Private** and it defines whether the rule is
 shared among other users or not.
 


 The parameter **default_status** changes the default status of Shared rules and/or
 Built-in rules for the requesting user's account. This parameter requires Account Manager privileges.
 


 The parameters **enable** and **send_mail** can be used to enable rules for
 the requesting user and set the notification preferences. When used in conjunction with the
 **user_id** parameter, an Account Manager can change these settings for their managed users as well.
 



**Examples**

Change the name of YARA Ruleset ID **123** to **Some New Name**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_name=Some+New+Name' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Update rules of YARA Ruleset ID **123**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_rules=%2F%2F+Commented+out+rules' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Update owner of YARA Ruleset ID **123** to **456**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_owner_user_id=456' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Update the type of YARA Ruleset ID **123** to **Shared**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_type=Shared' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Update the type of YARA Ruleset ID **123** to **Private**:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_type=Private' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Update the default status of YARA Ruleset ID **123** for my account (Account Manager only):
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_default_status=True' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Enable YARA Ruleset ID **123** for the current user:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_enable=True' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
Enable YARA Ruleset ID **123** for the current user and update notification settings:
```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
    'https://<YOUR_HOSTNAME_HERE>/rest/yara/123?yara_ruleset_enable=True&yara_ruleset_send_mail=True' \
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```

```bash
    -H 'Authorization: api_key <YOUR_APIKEY_HERE>'
```
